title: Club Career
text:
2015 — AS Monaco debut. Makes his senior debut in December 2015 at age 16, becoming the club’s youngest-ever first-team player.


2016–17 — Breakout season. Helps Monaco win the Ligue 1 title and reach the Champions League semi-finals, finishing as joint-top scorer in the league and winning the Ligue 1 Young Player of the Year award.


2017 — Move to Paris Saint-Germain. Joins PSG initially on loan, then permanently for 2018, in a transfer reported around €180 million — at the time the second-most expensive transfer in history and the most expensive for a teenager.


2018–2024 — PSG dominance. Becomes the focal point of PSG’s attack, winning multiple Ligue 1 titles, several Coupe de France and Trophée des Champions titles, and reaching the 2020 UEFA Champions League final. Repeatedly finishes as Ligue 1’s top scorer.


2024 — Free transfer to Real Madrid. Leaves PSG at the end of his contract and joins Real Madrid on a free transfer, fulfilling a long-rumoured move and taking the number 9 shirt.


2024–present — Real Madrid. Continues his career at the Santiago Bernabéu, adding to his individual scoring records and pursuing further domestic and European silverware.

title: Club Career
text:
AS Monaco (2015–2017)
Mbappé progressed rapidly through Monaco’s academy, one of the most productive in Europe, before establishing himself in the senior side. His standout 2016–17 campaign — including standout performances against clubs like Manchester City in the Champions League — made him one of the most coveted young talents in world football.

title: Club Career
text:
Paris Saint-Germain (2017–2024)
At PSG, Mbappé formed a formidable attacking partnership first with Neymar and Edinson Cavani, and later with Lionel Messi and Neymar in a trio nicknamed “MNM.” Over seven seasons in the French capital he:

Won the Ligue 1 title multiple times, becoming a fixture of PSG’s domestic dominance.
Won several Coupe de France and Trophée des Champions titles.
Reached the 2020 UEFA Champions League final, PSG’s first, where they lost to Bayern Munich.
Repeatedly won the Ligue 1 top scorer award and PSG’s Player of the Year honours.
Became PSG’s all-time leading goalscorer, surpassing club legend Edinson Cavani’s record.

His time at PSG was also marked by prolonged transfer speculation, most notably a widely reported interest from Real Madrid across multiple transfer windows, before he ultimately signed a contract extension in 2022 and then departed as a free agent in 2024.

title: Club Career
text:
Real Madrid (2024–present)
Mbappé’s arrival at Real Madrid in the summer of 2024 ended years of speculation about a move to the Spanish giants. Wearing the number 9 shirt, he joined a squad already featuring stars such as Vinícius Júnior, Jude Bellingham, and Rodrygo, forming one of the most feared attacking line-ups in world football. His debut season in Spain saw him quickly adapt to La Liga, contributing heavily to Real Madrid’s goal tally in domestic and European competition.
See Honours & Records for a full list of his club trophies and individual awards.

title: International Career
text: Mbappé progressed through France’s youth national teams before earning his first senior call-up in 2017. He made his senior debut for France that year and quickly became a first-team regular under manager Didier Deschamps.

title: International Career
text: Mbappé progressed through France’s youth national teams before earning his first senior call-up in 2017. He made his senior debut for France that year and quickly became a first-team regular under manager Didier Deschamps.

title: International Career
text:
2018 FIFA World Cup — Champion
Selected for the 2018 World Cup in Russia at just 19 years old, Mbappé announced himself on the world stage:

Scored a memorable goal in the Round of 16 against Argentina, drawing a penalty and scoring himself in a thrilling 4–3 win — the performance that made global headlines.
Scored in the final as France beat Croatia 4–2, helping secure France’s second World Cup title — becoming the youngest player to score in a World Cup final since Pelé in 1958.
Won the tournament’s Best Young Player award.


“I told myself: whatever happens, I have to enjoy it, because these are moments you dream about your whole life.” — Kylian Mbappé, on the 2018 World Cup

title: International Career
text:
UEFA Euro 2020 (played 2021)
France entered as reigning World Cup champions but exited in the Round of 16 to Switzerland on penalties, a shootout in which Mbappé missed the decisive kick — a rare setback that he has since spoken about as a formative experience.

title: International Career
section: 2022 FIFA World Cup — Runner-up, Golden Boot
text:
2022 FIFA World Cup — Runner-up, Golden Boot
Mbappé was at the heart of France’s run to a second consecutive World Cup final in Qatar:

Finished as the tournament’s top scorer, winning the Golden Boot with 8 goals.
Scored a hat-trick in the final against Argentina, becoming only the second player ever — after Geoff Hurst in 1966 — to score three goals in a World Cup final, in a match widely regarded as one of the greatest ever played.
France ultimately lost the final on penalties after a 3–3 draw.

title: International Career
text:
UEFA Euro 2024
Mbappé captained France at Euro 2024 in Germany, playing much of the tournament wearing a protective mask after fracturing his nose in the opening match. France reached the semi-finals before being eliminated.

title: International Career
text:
Captaincy and records
Mbappé has served as France’s captain and, over his international career, has climbed toward the top of France’s all-time goalscoring charts, closing in on and eventually surpassing longstanding national records held by past legends of the French game.
See Honours & Records for the complete list of international titles and individual awards.

title: Kylian Mbappé
text:
Who is Kylian Mbappé?
Kylian Mbappé Lottin is a French professional footballer widely regarded as one of the best players of his generation. Renowned for his explosive pace, clinical finishing, and dribbling ability, he rose from the youth academy at AS Monaco to become a World Cup champion, a serial Ligue 1 title winner with Paris Saint-Germain, and — since the summer of 2024 — a Real Madrid forward.
He is the youngest Frenchman to score at a World Cup since Pelé, and in the 2022 World Cup final he became the first player since Geoff Hurst in 1966 to score a hat-trick in a World Cup final.

“I have always dreamed big. When you dream, you have to dream big — otherwise it isn’t worth dreaming at all.” — Kylian Mbappé

title: Biography
text:
Kylian Mbappé Lottin was born on December 20, 1998, in Paris and grew up in Bondy, a suburb northeast of the city, in the Seine-Saint-Denis department. Football ran in the family: his father, Wilfried, coached the local club AS Bondy, where Kylian played as a boy, while his mother, Fayza Lamari, was a former handball player. His younger brother, Ethan, is also a professional footballer, and his adopted older brother, Jires Kembo Ekoko, played professionally in Africa and Europe.
From a young age, Mbappé stood out for his speed and self-belief. He trained at the Clairefontaine academy — the French national football institute — before being snapped up by several major European clubs. He ultimately chose AS Monaco, joining their academy in 2013 over offers from clubs including Real Madrid, in part so he could continue his footballing development close to home while finishing his studies.

title: Biography
text:
Kylian Mbappé Lottin was born on December 20, 1998, in Paris and grew up in Bondy, a suburb northeast of the city, in the Seine-Saint-Denis department. Football ran in the family: his father, Wilfried, coached the local club AS Bondy, where Kylian played as a boy, while his mother, Fayza Lamari, was a former handball player. His younger brother, Ethan, is also a professional footballer, and his adopted older brother, Jires Kembo Ekoko, played professionally in Africa and Europe.
From a young age, Mbappé stood out for his speed and self-belief. He trained at the Clairefontaine academy — the French national football institute — before being snapped up by several major European clubs. He ultimately chose AS Monaco, joining their academy in 2013 over offers from clubs including Real Madrid, in part so he could continue his footballing development close to home while finishing his studies.

title: Biography
text:
Breaking through at Monaco
Mbappé signed his first professional contract with Monaco in 2015 and made his senior debut in December of that year, becoming the youngest player in Monaco’s history. His breakout came in the 2016–17 season, when, still a teenager, he became a key attacking threat as Monaco won the Ligue 1 title and reached the semi-finals of the UEFA Champions League. He finished the season as Ligue 1’s joint-top scorer and was named the league’s Young Player of the Year.
That season announced him to the world: a teenager combining searing pace, composure in front of goal, and a football IQ well beyond his years.

title: Biography
text:
A defining choice
In the summer of 2017, Mbappé chose to join Paris Saint-Germain rather than a host of Europe’s traditional superpowers — a decision that placed him alongside Neymar in one of the most expensive attacking line-ups ever assembled, and set the stage for a decade at the top of the sport.

“Bondy made me who I am.” — Kylian Mbappé, on his hometown

title: Biography
text:
Personal life
Mbappé has become known not only for his performances on the pitch but for his outspokenness on social issues, his active charitable foundation supporting underprivileged children, and his business ventures off the pitch. He has spoken about the importance of education, having insisted as a teenager on including a clause in his contracts to continue schooling alongside his football career.
For the story of what came next, see Club Career and International.
